chapter: Joining Earl Hines and the Grand Terrace
title: Arranging pop tunes for publishers; George Dixon fronts the band
summary: Publishers paid arrangers; Dixon conducted when Hines was off the stand.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, at the Grand Terrace, you did a lot of arrangements for -- you said that was the first you got into the full band arrangements.
What were some of the things you arranged?

I can't remember too many of them. A lot of the arranging we did was popular music. Back in them days they didn't have the guys, you know, to come around singing and going on, what'd they call them, tune pluggers. You didn't have them back in them days. So the different representatives from the publishing companies would come by Grand Terrace, and each one of them had their own arrangement -- own arranger. They'd pick out to do arranging on a new tune they got coming out. So I did a lot of those, Budd Johnson did a lot of them, Jimmy Mundy did a lot of them, and then --
Cecil Irwin did some arranging, too, didn't he?
Cecil Irwin did some arrangements before he got killed.
Did you get extra pay for that?
No, the publishing company paid you for that.
Did they pay Earl to play it on the radio?
No. After we made the arrangement, we just goed ahead and played.
Did Earl have a straw boss at the Grand Terrace? I mean, somebody run the band, or did he, you know, call the tunes?
Oh, well -- no, he had a -- you wouldn't call him a straw boss. George Dixon used to conduct the band when Earl was off the stand.
But would Earl call the sets, or would George?
George called the sets. When Earl come on the stand, then he'd call the sets.
